newsitem.title: FINLAND: PTT WARNS OF RISKS OF MARKKA IN SINGLE CURRENCY.
newsitem.headline: PTT WARNS OF RISKS OF MARKKA IN SINGLE CURRENCY.

text.p: If a recession as severe as the one in the early 1990s had struck with the markka irrevocably fixed to Europe's single euro currency, the Finnish jobless rate could have risen to 30 percent, Pellervo economic research institute PTT said on Wednesday.

Without the November 1991 devaluation and September 1992 float of the markka, the slump in Finnish GDP in 1991-94 would have been 23 percent instead of the 13 percent fall which materialised, PTT said.

"In an euro world this alternative (devaluation) would not have existed and an exceptionally big country-specific cyclical disturbance like the one experienced would have led to unemployment of over 750,000 people or 30 percent," PTT said.
It referred to a study made by its retired managing director, economics professor Pertti Kukkonen.

PTT is close to the Central Union of Agricultural Producers and Forest Owners (MTK), and to the opposition Centre Party -- both of which are critical of the Finnish left-right-green government's drive to see Finland in the starting group of the third stage of European economic and monetary union in 1999.
